messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]

L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]

S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]

picks.reason: Tests whether the strong CsOAc/XPhos/butyronitrile result persists at the intermediate concentration.
Measures the low-concentration effect under the best observed base, ligand, solvent, and temperature.
Checks whether lowering temperature improves on the 84.6% result at the highest concentration.
Tests the higher-temperature condition at intermediate concentration with the leading base and ligand.
Completes the low-concentration temperature comparison for the leading base and ligand.
Tests the lower-temperature condition at intermediate concentration to map the concentration–temperature interaction.
Completes the low-concentration temperature comparison and checks whether dilution changes the temperature optimum.
Tests whether cesium acetate improves the xylene result relative to the butyronitrile benchmark.
Screens butyl acetate against the strong butyronitrile conditions while holding other factors fixed.
Screens BrettPhos under the best observed reaction conditions as a plausible bulky biaryl-phosphine alternative.
Tests whether the bulky electron-rich JackiePhos ligand can outperform XPhos under optimized conditions.
Evaluates a strongly donating trialkylphosphine ligand under the leading reaction conditions.
Provides a conventional triphenylphosphine comparison under the best observed base, solvent, and temperature.
Screens the structurally distinct CgMe-PPh ligand under the optimized conditions.
Tests the smaller, more electron-rich PPhMe2 ligand under conditions that maximize the current lead.
Reassesses PPh2Me under the optimized conditions because its prior test used a different base, solvent, concentration, and temperature.
Screens the electron-rich furyl phosphine under the best observed reaction conditions.
Checks whether the low prior GorlosPhos result was due to its earlier conditions rather than the ligand.
Reassesses tBPh-CPhos under optimized conditions because its earlier low yield was measured at low concentration and higher temperature.
Tests whether the previously unsuccessful PPhtBu2 combination benefits from the leading solvent, concentration, and temperature.
